Here, we employ a recently described data-driven voxel-wise connectivity analysis, intrinsic connectivity distribution (ICD) ( ), to identify between-group differences and correlations with self-reported food-craving ratings.
Group-level two tailed t -tests were used to compare groups (PCE and NDE) and conditions (favorite-food, stress and neutral) in ICD connectivity.

description.value: Functional images were slice-time and motion corrected using SPM5. Trials exceeding the specified motion thresholds were excluded; linear and quadratic drift, six rigid-body motion parameters, mean CSF, white-matter, and global signals were regressed out. A gray-matter mask was applied, imagery-period data were concatenated by condition, ICD maps were normalized to each subject's mean and standard deviation, smoothed with a 6-mm Gaussian kernel, and registered to common template space using BioImage Suite.

spans.text: Images were slice-time and motion corrected using SPM5 ( http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk ). Trials with linear motion of ± 1.5 mm or with a rotation of >2° were excluded.

name.value: individualized guided imagery with appetitive, stressful and neutral-relaxing cue scripts

description.value: Participants underwent individualized imagery scripts of appetitive, stressful and neutral-relaxing content during fMRI scanning.

spans.text: All adolescents participated in a well-validated imagery task ( ) composed of 2-min individualized imagery scripts of appetitive, stressful or neutral-relaxing content.

description.value: Participants imagined having their favorite food in front of them and mentally engaged with the appetitive script for 2 minutes followed by 0.5 minutes of quiet passive imagery; two favorite-food trials were presented.

Participants mentally and physically engaged with an individualized stressful personal-experience script for 2 minutes followed by 0.5 minutes of quiet passive imagery; two stressful trials were presented.

Participants mentally and physically engaged with an individualized neutral-relaxing personal-experience script for 2 minutes followed by 0.5 minutes of quiet passive imagery; two neutral-relaxing trials were presented and this condition served as the active control.

value: speech

spans.text: Participants responded verbally using a Likert scale from 0 to 10

instructions.value: During script imagery, participants were instructed to mentally and physically engage in the individualized scripts based on prior out-of-scanner training. During baseline and recovery periods they were instructed to lie still in the scanner; during baseline they were instructed not to engage in any specific mental activity, and during recovery they remained still until craving matched the baseline rating.

spans.text: During script imagery, participants were instructed to mentally and physically engage in the scripts based on prior out-of-scanner training.

stimuli.value: Clinician-recorded, individualized 2-minute audiotaped imagery scripts describing each participant's favorite food, a stressful personal experience, or a neutral-relaxing personal experience.

spans.text: Each script was based on a personal experience described by participants, developed using the scene development questionnaire ( ) and audiotaped by a clinician for presentation during the fMRI session.
